html:
The Margraviate of Brandenburg was a state of the Holy Roman Empire around Berlin in northeast Germany, ruled from 1415 by the Hohenzollern family. On the map for 1715 it is the core of the rising Prussian state.

Its rulers were electors, among the princes who chose the emperor. Brandenburg suffered terribly in the Thirty Years' War. Then Frederick William, the "Great Elector", rebuilt it, built a standing army and in 1685 invited French Protestant refugees to settle. In 1618 the Hohenzollerns had also inherited the Duchy of Prussia, outside the Empire. In 1701 the Great Elector's son crowned himself King in Prussia in Königsberg, and the joined lands became known as Prussia.

In 1715 the king was Frederick William I, the "soldier king", who built up the army and treasury that his son Frederick the Great would use.
